# A second tag returning typed errors makes the generated barrel ambiguous

- **Reported-in:** linkedin-challenge (migrating to the `.nextrs/` client layout)
- **Date:** 2026-08-15
- **Status:** fixed in 3ca0527

## Problem

`emit_barrel` writes one line per tag:

```ts
// @generated by nextrs::bundle (every build). Do not edit by hand.
export * from "./me/me";
export * from "./orgs/orgs";
```

Since the `ApiError` convention landed, orval copies its shared HTTP status
helpers into **every tag module that returns a typed error**, verbatim:

```ts
export type HTTPStatusCode1xx = 100 | 101 | 102 | 103;
// … 2xx, 3xx, 4xx, 5xx …
export type HTTPStatusCodes = HTTPStatusCode1xx | HTTPStatusCode2xx | …;
```

Two such tags therefore declare the same six names, and starring both is
ambiguous. TypeScript rejects the barrel with TS2308 — once per duplicated name,
per entry point, so an app with two tags gets twelve errors:

```
src/generated/fetch/index.ts:12:1 - error TS2308: Module "./me/me" has already
exported a member named 'HTTPStatusCode1xx'. Consider explicitly re-exporting to
resolve the ambiguity.
```

The blast radius is larger than the message suggests. `tsc` runs with
`noEmitOnError`, so the generated package never produces `dist/`. Its `exports`
map points every entry at `dist/*.js` and `dist/*.d.ts`, so **every consumer of
the client sees an unresolvable module** — pages, the app's `typecheck` script,
and the editor all report `Cannot find module "@app/client/react-query"`. Nothing
in that symptom points back at a barrel the developer never wrote and is told not
to edit.

`react-todos` cannot reproduce it: one tag cannot collide with itself. The bug
is invisible in-repo and unavoidable in any real app, which is roughly the worst
combination — the first thing an adopter hits is a wall of errors in generated
code, attributable to nothing they did.

## Resolution

The first tag to declare a name claims it. Tags that add only fresh names keep
their `export *`; a tag carrying a duplicate re-exports its own names explicitly
instead:

```ts
export * from "./me/me";
export { getOrg, useGetOrg } from "./orgs/orgs";
export type { getOrgResponse, GetOrgQueryResult } from "./orgs/orgs";
```

Two details that are easy to get wrong:

- **Types and values need separate statements.** Listing a type in a value
  `export { … }` typechecks — `tsc` resolves it fine — but the bundler erases
  types before it resolves the barrel, so there is no runtime binding to find and
  rolldown fails the build with `MISSING_EXPORT`. This only surfaces at
  `bundle_pages` time, well after the client package builds cleanly, so the two
  failures look unrelated. `enum` counts as a value; `type` and `interface` do
  not.
- **Reading a module must be best-effort.** An unreadable or unrecognized module
  contributes no names and leaves the caller on a plain `export *` — the
  pre-existing behavior, and the right fallback for a torn generated dir.

Name extraction is a line scanner rather than a parser. The input is
machine-written in a narrow set of shapes (`export type|const|interface|function|
enum|class`, always column zero, one declaration per line), and the only consumer
is the duplicate check.

## Validation

- `client_barrel_resolves_names_two_tags_both_declare` — two tags declaring a
  shared name: the first keeps `export *`, the second names only what it adds,
  split across value and type statements.
- `exported_names_reads_orval_declaration_shapes` — every declaration form orval
  emits, with the type/value split; indented `export` inside a namespace is not
  part of the surface; a missing module yields nothing.
- Existing barrel tests still pass with empty tag dirs, which exercise the
  best-effort fallback.
- End to end in linkedin-challenge (15 tags, two of them carrying typed errors):
  `cargo nextrs client generate`, `npm run typecheck`, and
  `cargo check --all-targets` all clean, and `dist/` emits.

## Worth considering separately

The duplication is orval's, not ours — it has no notion of a shared preamble
module in `tags-split` mode. Deduping at the barrel is the cheap fix and the one
that belongs in the framework. Hoisting the helpers into `model/` during codegen
would be tidier output, but it means rewriting generated tag modules after orval
runs, which is a much larger commitment to owning that output.

See also [Generated client barrel exports](generated-client-barrel-exports.md),
which introduced the generated barrel.
